sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case N08: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 241x241x267 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case N08 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(241, 241, 267) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: peripheral nerve sheath tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 133/267 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I can see the bright mass on the left side in the axial view. Let me scan through the full set of axial slices to confirm its location and extent.

content.thinking: I'm trying to locate the mass in the thigh—there seems to be a lateral lesion near the femur with heterogeneous, target-like signal around slices 118-176, and a separate posterior-medial rounded structure at slices 162-220 that might just be vessels rather than the nerve sheath tumor itself. I need to figure out which one is actually the nerve lesion.

content.text: sheet coronal 70–190/241 (12 slices) | v0 | tool calls 3/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm trying to estimate the lesion's vertical extent in the coronal view by working out the pixel-to-slice scale, but it's easier to just look at the axial slice directly, starting around slice 133 with the marks shown.

content.text: axial 133/267 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 4/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm noticing mark 484 sits near the left edge of the lesion, so I should crop more tightly around that region to get a better view.

content.text: axial 133/267 | crop marks | marks fine | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 5/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'll just use a single point marker at 1130, centered inside the lesion, rather than trying to box it.

content.text: version v1 (parent v0) | volume 30.1 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 106–193, coronal 111–143, sagittal 50–77 | change +30.1 mL / 0.0 mL | tool calls 6/40, prompts 1/15 | point add (1 mark(s)) | image: axial 146, coronal 127, sagittal 63 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: The lesion spans axial slices 106-193, which is quite long, but I want to check whether the tumor tapers along the nerve and possibly extends further beyond this range. I should look at specific slices like 110, 118, 165, 185, and 193 to verify the mask boundaries.

content.text: sheet axial 96–206/267 (12 slices) | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
The slice indexing probably runs from distal to proximal, so that's not critical. The mask itself looks reasonable, though I'm now wondering about the posterior mass spanning slices 176-220 near the sciatic nerve region — that round, bright ~10mm structure on 186-206 could represent the nerve itself or possibly another nerve sheath tumor.

Could this posterior finding be a vessel like the popliteal vein instead, or is it a separate lesion from the lateral mass? The lateral mass sits in the intermuscular septum between vastus lateralis and biceps femoris, lateral to the femur, which makes me think it's more likely the primary peripheral nerve sheath tumor, while the posterior blob may just be the sciatic nerve or an adjacent vessel. I want to cross-check this posterior blob against coronal and sagittal views to clarify its identity.

I'm trying to figure out the exact voxel coordinates by cross-referencing panel positions across the axial, coronal, and sagittal views, but the array dimensions and indexing conventions seem inconsistent between views, making it hard to pin down whether the lesion's coronal and sagittal extents genuinely overlap.

I'll stop guessing at pixel math and instead just directly view coronal slice 144 to check the posterior blob location.

content.text: axial 196/267 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 8/40, prompts 1/15
axial 166/267 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 9/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm comparing panels across slices—noting the first image had no mask at all, while at slice 166 the segmentation seems to miss a bright crescent region and a nearby blob that could be the sciatic nerve. At slice 196, I'm also spotting a round bright structure that looks like it might be the sciatic nerve too.

Though it could be the tibial nerve branch rather than the sciatic nerve itself, given the rim hyperintensity. I'm tracking the trajectory of this blob across slices—it starts as a small ring, grows brighter and rounder through the middle slices, which makes me wonder if it's actually a second, separate lesion rather than just a normal nerve structure, especially given the possibility this is a multifocal process. I should check the coronal/sagittal views to clarify.

content.text: axial 166/267 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The mask seems to be missing that bright posterior region, since the lesion's full ovoid shape includes that crescent. I think I should try placing a positive point directly on the bright crescent and see if the model extends the segmentation to include it, using the crop mask with marks view to check.

content.text: axial 166/267 | crop mask | marks fine | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 11/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: I notice mark 1179 sits on the bright crescent, so adding a positive point there could capture that whole bright region. Since there aren't enough marks along the boundary to use a lasso effectively, I'll go with a point instead.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 32.5 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 106–192, coronal 111–143, sagittal 50–77 | change +2.6 mL / -0.1 mL | tool calls 12/40, prompts 2/15 | point add (1 mark(s)) | image: axial 147, coronal 127, sagittal 63 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: I'm trying to reconcile the axial and coronal slice ranges to figure out where the lesion actually sits in the image, since the voxel coordinates across views don't seem to line up cleanly yet.

content.text: axial 166/267 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 13/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: Good overall fit, including the posterior tail which could be a vessel or edema but seems acceptable. Now I need to check the top and bottom ends against the mask extent spanning rows 104–194.

content.text: sheet axial 100–122/267 (8 slices) | v2 | tool calls 14/40, prompts 2/15
sheet axial 172–200/267 (8 slices) | v2 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
Looking at slices 100-106, I notice a bright oval that shifts position across these slices — likely a vessel like the femoral or popliteal vein rather than the actual lesion. The mask itself tapers at both ends with thin tails, which seems consistent with normal anatomy.

I should check whether the inferior tail at slices 106-109 is a genuine finding, since tumors near nerves often taper naturally like this. Now I want to verify the lateral boundary in the middle slices — 126, 136, 156 — since 136 and 146 already looked fine, and the coronal view showed a clean tapering at the superior end. Let me zoom into axial slices 126 and 156 to double-check before finishing the review.

content.text: axial 150/267 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 16/40, prompts 2/15
axial 124/267 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 17/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
The mask picks up a bit of extra anterior-lateral tissue near the fascia — a slight overshoot that could be trimmed with a morphological opening, but it's tolerable. In slice 150, the mask extends into a gray wedge lateral to the bright core, likely representing the lesion's periphery or pseudo-capsule, which seems acceptable to keep.

I consider using a small opening operation to remove thin protrusions, but it feels risky and unnecessary here, so I'll skip it and move on to wrap up the review.

arguments.reason: Lateral T2-bright lobulated mass segmented and checked in three planes

content.text:
Final review of v2: volume 32.5 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 106–192, coronal 111–143, sagittal 50–77 | tool calls 18/40, prompts 2/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).
C1 add 74 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly left of the mask
C2 add 68 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly left of the mask
C3 add 58 mL, touches mask on its right, left and posterior sides, mostly superior of the mask
C4 add 6.6 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly superior of the mask
C5 add 3.0 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "1587" to save it.

content.thinking: These candidates are just subcutaneous fat, nothing abnormal, so I'll reject them. Looking back at axial slices 128 and 149, I notice an anterior-lateral wedge extension at the corner that fits—this one works, so I'm done.

arguments.reason: Lateral T2-bright lobulated mass outlined well in all three planes with tapering ends. The candidates were fat or normal tissue, so I rejected them. A separate posterior blob was judged to be the sciatic nerve and left out, which is a minor uncertainty.

content.text: case N08 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v2 | final volume 32.5 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 19/40, prompts 2/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I saved the segmentation of the peripheral nerve sheath tumor, a single component of 32.5 mL. I'm rating confidence as medium.

- **What I segmented:** the bright, lobulated mass on the patient's left side of the thigh, next to the femur. It runs over axial slices 106–192 and tapers at both ends.
- **How:** one positive point on the mass, then a second point on its bright posterior crescent, which the first pass had missed. That was 2 of the 15 model prompts. I checked the outline in axial, coronal and sagittal views and in the final review.
- **Rejected candidates:** the five automatic proposals in the final review were subcutaneous fat or normal tissue, so I did not add any of them.
- **Main uncertainty:** a separate, rounder bright structure sits in the posterior thigh, behind the femoral vessels, over roughly slices 156–220. I judged it to be the sciatic nerve and left it out, but it could be a second lesion.
- **Minor overshoot:** on some slices the outline includes a thin wedge of grey tissue on the anterior-lateral edge. I read it as tumor periphery and kept it, but it may be slightly generous.
